_comment: Verify this schema against your installed version with /hooks before trusting it. Hook config shape has changed between Claude Code releases.
_permissions_allow_note: Two entries in permissions.allow are worth explaining, so an allow-list review does not re-derive them. Bash(npm run lint) CANNOT SUCCEED TODAY — there is no package.json — and it is kept ON PURPOSE, because it becomes true at build-order step 7 when the Vite app lands. That is exactly what distinguishes it from Bash(make check), REMOVED 2026-08-11: make check runs lint and typecheck, both stubs that exit 1 by design (see the header comment in the Makefile — a target that exits 0 with nothing to run is a lie), so it can never exit 0, and nothing automated invokes it. One impossible grant resolves itself; the other does not. Bash(make status) and Bash(make docs-audit) were added in the same edit — both read-only, and status is what README.md and CLAUDE.md tell a cold session to run first. Deliberately NOT granted: make audit-history, a slow once-in-a-while diagnostic that a standing grant would invite into routine use.
_PreToolUse_opsec_note: RE-ENABLED 2026-08-23, discharging D16's 'revisit before the codes track handles real cards' — D24's build made that condition true. It was off from 2026-08-03 because it blocked any write containing a code-shaped literal, including placeholders in prose about the format: two blocked writes in one session. The fix is what D16 prescribed, a narrower pattern and never a toggle: a candidate now blocks only when it stands alone (not flanked by a letter, digit or hyphen), mixes letters AND digits, and has no group that is one repeated character — so the all-X layout, letters-only examples, digit runs and windows inside longer chains all pass, and every reconstructed historical false positive was verified passing before this entry was written. Context exclusions (.md files, comment lines) were considered and rejected: prose is where a real code is likeliest to leak. The guard FAILS OPEN — any internal error, missing python3, or malformed payload exits 0 — because a guard that blocks on its own bugs gets disabled again, and the pre-commit hook keeps the deliberately BROAD twin of this rule as the commit-time backstop for the ~2% of real codes the narrow shape lets through. Budget arithmetic is in the script's own header.
_PreToolUse_decision_context_note: ADDED with D16/D17. scripts/decision-context.py names the settled decisions governing the file about to be edited, read out of docs/map.py and summarised from docs/DECISIONS.md itself so no summary can drift from its decision. It exits 0 unconditionally — on bad input, a missing map, or its own bugs — and prints nothing for files no map entry covers, which is most of them. It is advisory and must never be able to fail an edit; that is the difference between it and the guard below, which over-triggered and was off within a day. It emits hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext rather than permissionDecision: setting permissionDecision to 'allow' would auto-approve every Write and Edit in the project, which is a security change wearing a convenience hat. If a Claude Code release ignores additionalContext the JSON is merely printed, so the failure mode is a lost nudge and never a blocked edit — CLAUDE.md points at docs/map.py directly for that reason.
_PostToolUse_typecheck_note: RE-ADDED 2026-08-12 with build-order step 6, when TypeScript arrived. This channel existed before and was deleted 2026-08-11: it ran `make lint typecheck`, both stubs that exit 1 by design, the abort on lint meant typecheck never ran, and a pipe to tail swallowed the status — five lines of failure text after every edit for eight days, blocking nothing. The fix is not a better target, it is that a hook matcher cannot filter by file path but the hook itself can. scripts/typecheck-hook.py reads the payload and exits 0 in silence unless the written file is a .ts or .tsx under app/, so editing markdown or Python spawns no process at all. It calls the compiler directly rather than `make typecheck`, whose NPM_GUARD install hint is right for a human and noise for a hook. Failure exits 2 with tsc's output on stderr; every other outcome — bad payload, no node_modules, its own bugs — exits 0 silently. It CANNOT block a write: PostToolUse fires after the tool has run.
_SessionStart_worktree_note: ADDED 2026-08-29. A git worktree gets the TRACKED files and nothing else, so .venv/, harness/.cache/ and app/node_modules/ — all gitignored by deliberate decision — do not travel to one. The three harness failures that causes name numpy, a fixture's internals and an empty cache, and not one of them contains the word 'worktree': a session lands in a fresh tree and spends its turn diagnosing the environment. A DEVCONTAINER DOES NOT FIX THIS and was considered: postCreateCommand fires when a container is created, while these worktrees are made by `git worktree add` inside one existing checkout, so it would never fire for them. SessionStart is the event that actually means 'somebody is about to work in this tree'. The hook copies harness/.cache (instant, local, and the one whose absence can cost MONEY — it is what T1 replays instead of submitting), builds .venv, and only REPORTS the ~80 MB npm install, per the Makefile's own NPM_GUARD argument that an implicit install hides a slow network step. It FAILS OPEN on every path including its own bugs, which is the rule guard-opsec.sh taught this repo the hard way. It writes, so D18 keeps it off the commit path: session start only, never `make check` and never the git hook.
_PreToolUse_kill_note: ADDED 2026-09-10, after two incidents in one session. A session cleaning up dev servers it had itself started ran `pkill -f "capture_server.py"` — machine-wide, so it also matched the owner's live capture server on :8000 over their real store, the process D53 exists to keep alive — and then `for p in $(lsof -ti tcp:5439); do kill $p; done`, where `lsof -ti` returns CLIENTS as well as listeners and the second pid was the desktop app's network helper. Three session notes already warned about this class and it happened twice anyway; a note that has to be remembered is not a guard. scripts/reap.py --hook RESOLVES the command's actual targets — running pgrep and lsof itself, read-only — and refuses when a target does not live under this checkout, which is the whole rule: everything an agent session may kill was started BY that session and lives under the tree it is working in. So `pkill -f capture_server.py` is ALLOWED when the only match is yours and refused when it is not, which no reading of the string could decide. It fails open on its own bugs — guard-opsec.sh's rule beside it, for guard-opsec.sh's reason — and fails CLOSED on a target it cannot place: the first is the guard being wrong about itself, the second is it being right that it does not know. The escape hatch is PKMNSCAN_KILL=off and every refusal prints it. D18 keeps its self-test off the commit path and in `make check`, beside janitor-selftest. D127.
_PreToolUse_silent_write_note: ADDED 2026-09-12, after a coordinator session reported work as landed that had not landed, twice in one session, through one command shape: `git commit -q -F - >/dev/null 2>&1 <<'EOF'`. The pre-commit hook REFUSED the commit, the refusal went to /dev/null, and the session then read `git log --oneline -1`, saw the PREVIOUS commit — a real commit with a real subject — and reported 'pushed'. The push that followed said `Everything up-to-date`, which read as success too. Nine instances of the class landed in about twenty-four hours, and a rule had already been written for it by the session that then broke it, which is why this is a hook. Both halves of that command are load-bearing: `2>/dev/null` hides every byte the pre-commit hook prints, and `>/dev/null` hides `[branch sha]`, the only positive proof a commit happened. So the predicate is not a list of redirection spellings — it is that a git WRITE must leave a trace the session can read, and discarding either of its own standard streams means the reader can no longer tell 'nothing is wrong' from 'nothing is known yet'. The roster is deliberately short (commit, push, pull, merge, rebase, cherry-pick, a fetch carrying a local refspec, `make merge`, `gh pr merge`) because every verb is false-positive surface: reads pass, `--dry-run` passes, `--abort` and `--quit` pass, and a quoted `>/dev/null` inside a commit message is a STRING rather than an operator, which is why the parser is shlex with punctuation_chars and never a regular expression. It fails OPEN on its own bugs — reap.py's asymmetry beside it, for reap.py's reason — and there is no fail-CLOSED case, because a command it cannot tokenize is one it has no opinion about. The escape hatch is PKMNSCAN_SILENT=off, honoured in the environment and inline, and printed in every refusal. D18 keeps its self-test off the commit path and in `make check`, beside reap-selftest.
_PreToolUse_guard_shell_note: ADDED 2026-09-12, out of a fourteen-agent read-only audit of every rule this repo has written down and broken anyway. scripts/guard-shell.py --hook carries eight clauses and each one has a measured incident behind it. (1) `git checkout <path>` / `git restore <path>` over a MODIFIED file: on 2026-09-06 one `git checkout cli/cmd_reprice.py` put a mutation back and destroyed ~240 lines of that session's uncommitted work, and the same command was typed again on 2026-09-12 over CLAUDE.md by a session with that rule in its own memory file. (2) A write outside this checkout: on 2026-09-06 an absolute-path `cd` prefix wrote ~1,500 lines into the owner's MAIN tree on `main`, and `make launch-agent`'s supervisor hot-reloaded that uncommitted branch code into their live :8000 capture server while they were using the app over their real store (D43). (3) `gh api -f k=v` with no method: a field implies a body, so gh sends POST, and on 2026-09-12 a GET spelled that way hung past a 120s tool timeout and left a process to reap. (4) `ln -s` at a path that already exists: on 2026-08-29 that created harness/images/images instead of failing, a copy brought the symlink loop back, T1 died naming only the symptom, and iCloud renamed the real 133 MB directory to `images 2`, empty. (5) A polling loop: on 2026-09-12 a `pgrep -f` waiter never went false and a backgrounded while/sleep merge driver ran 119 rounds over 3h58m across a compaction of the session that started it, racing that session's own merges until a human noticed a four-hour bash in their UI. IT RESOLVES RATHER THAN PATTERN-MATCHES, which is reap.py's standard and the only way these questions have answers: `git checkout main` and `git checkout CLAUDE.md` differ only in the filesystem and `git status --porcelain`, `ln -s a b` is right or wrong depending on whether b exists, and a backgrounded script's loop is in the FILE rather than in the command — so the file is read. A subject it cannot resolve is a command it has no opinion about, and it says so rather than passing silently. IT IS ARMED ON Write|Edit AS WELL, and that half parses nothing at all: the target is resolved and compared against this checkout's root, so no shell form can skirt it. The user's own ~/.claude and a temp directory that is no checkout both pass; a temp directory that IS a checkout does not, which is what lets its own fixture pose the case. EIGHT HATCHES AND NOT ONE — PKMNSCAN_CHECKOUT, PKMNSCAN_TREE, PKMNSCAN_GH, PKMNSCAN_LINK, PKMNSCAN_WAIT, PKMNSCAN_PUSH, PKMNSCAN_STASH, PKMNSCAN_RESET — because a single switch would mean disarming the clause that guards uncommitted work in order to make a symlink. Each is honoured in the environment and inline, and printed in its own refusal. It fails OPEN on its own bugs, including a missing scripts/shell_parse.py, the tokenizer it shares with silent-write-guard.py. D18 keeps its self-test off the commit path and in `make check`, beside reap-selftest. AMENDED: clause 6 (a push to a differently-named upstream, PKMNSCAN_PUSH) landed 2026-09-13. Clauses 7 and 8 landed 2026-09-16 on the parent CLAUDE.md's shared-trees rule: (7) a bare `git stash`, a `pop`, or a `drop`/`clear` naming no entry, because the stash stack is per-CLONE and this clone runs ~30 working trees with live sessions in them, so an entry is very likely another session's; `git stash push -u -m <tag>`, `list`, `show` and `apply <sha>` pass. (8) `git reset --hard`/`--merge`/`--keep` over a tree holding uncommitted tracked changes, read from `git status --porcelain` the way clause 1 reads it; `--soft`, a bare mixed reset and a clean tree all pass, and the refusal names the `.bak` copy.
_SessionEnd_teardown_note: WorktreeRemove fires at the moment the tree goes, which is exactly the moment whose absence left four supervisors restarting against deleted directories on 2026-09-06 (D111). SessionEnd is the second anchor and the weaker one: it is not reliable at app quit or machine sleep, and its `reason` includes `clear`, where the session CONTINUES — the script skips that reason by name so it cannot stop a server somebody is still using. The timeout is raised because SessionEnd hooks share a 1.5s budget by default and `serve.py down` drains. It fails open on every path, and whatever it misses `make janitor` reaps later — which is the point of having a sweep that does not depend on an event. NOT on the commit path: D18.
